title: Seizure first aid
version: Epilepsy New Zealand poster 'Adult first aid for seizures' (2020 in the file name, no date printed) and web pages 'Seizure First Aid' and 'Tonic-clonic seizures' (no date shown, footer Copyright 2026); Hato Hone St John 'Seizures or convulsions' first aid library page (no date shown, footer 2025); ANZCOR Guideline 9.2.4 'First Aid Management of a Seizure' (Approved June 2024); KidsHealth NZ 'Febrile seizures in children' (Last reviewed 6 June 2024); all read 20 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Every site blocks direct download here (curl refused for epilepsy.org.nz, stjohn.org.nz, anzcor.org and kidshealth.org.nz) and web search gave titles only, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote exact lines (long sentences in pieces, rejoined). No PDF was in sources/. Sections: A Epilepsy NZ adult poster (main source; which column each poster line sits under is inferred from layout, and the 'call an ambulance 111 if' heading is a graphic), A2 Epilepsy NZ web pages (call-111 list, tonic-clonic do/do not, seizures in water; a few explanatory sentences were only paraphrased by the tool and are marked in brackets, focal/absence/wheelchair sections not captured), B Hato Hone St John NZ (whole first-aid text, key numbers confirmed in a second read), C ANZCOR 9.2.4 (joint Australia-NZ; summary, recognition, management, ambulance list, water, do not), D KidsHealth NZ febrile seizures in children (some headings are the tool's and some lines between were not captured; infographic heading unreadable). Differences: (1) not waking after the seizure: Epilepsy NZ and ANZCOR say call if not responsive/conscious within 5 minutes; St John says call if the person does not wake within 10 minutes; KidsHealth says call if the child is 'not waking up and responding' with no time. (2) All four say call 111 if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, but Epilepsy NZ's web page adds 'or follow the timing in their personal SMP', and St John says a person with epilepsy needs no ambulance unless it lasts more than 5 minutes, while Epilepsy NZ and ANZCOR also call for first seizure, no management plan, not knowing the person, pregnancy, water, injury, repeat seizure. St John's list is only 5 minutes, 10 minutes, not breathing well; St John alone mentions Healthline 0800 611 116 and seeing a doctor after a first seizure. (3) When to roll onto the side: the Epilepsy NZ poster says after jerking stops (or at once if food, fluid or vomit in mouth); the Epilepsy NZ web page says 'as soon as possible'; ANZCOR says turn on the side 'when practical' during, then recovery position once it stops; St John only after the seizure. (4) Timing: Epilepsy NZ, ANZCOR and KidsHealth say time the seizure; St John does not. (5) Febrile: St John says cool the child by removing clothing down to underwear or nappy; ANZCOR and KidsHealth say do not put the child in a bath (KidsHealth: or shower) to cool them; KidsHealth says loosen clothes around face and neck and video the seizure if you can. (6) Water: Epilepsy NZ says remove once the active movements have ceased; ANZCOR says as soon as it is safe. (7) Food and drink: Epilepsy NZ no water, food or pills unless fully alert; ANZCOR nothing to eat and drink until fully awake and alert; St John (febrile only) nothing to drink until fully conscious. Gaps: no source says what to do if the person is not breathing beyond ANZCOR's pointer to the basic life support flowchart; no source gives a time for a cluster or how long to stay; none covers rescue medicines in detail (ANZCOR says follow training and the plan); St John gives no 'do not' about food or drink for adults.
status: Reviewer: 5 instructions missed (incl. ease the fall, wheelchair brakes) and 14 findings, all fixed but 3 small ones. 119 of 119 quotes exact (web copy).
